paths.description: Homepage and primary browsing entry; global navigation, consent, responsive, performance and privacy conditions.
Category index archetype representing taxonomy navigation.
Ranked media listing archetype representing dense result grids.
Representative media detail page; metadata and playback surface.
Primary account-creation journey, email reveal and invalid submission state.
Deliberately invalid route to test runtime failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found eight running 2-second animations while matchMedia(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) was true.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduced-motion media query that removes or shortens non-essential animation.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not handled
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, and Lighthouse found 13 color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve system colors in forced-colors mode and provide a higher-contrast token set.

findings.summary: Route and state changes lack continuity cues
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition usage across the MPA navigation surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful navigation changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Scrolling enhancements are not compositor-driven
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no animation-timeline, scroll-timeline, or view-timeline usage on the long listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Where scroll-linked feedback is useful, use CSS scroll-driven animations rather than main-thread handlers.

findings.summary: Long media listings provide no gesture-oriented affordances
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no scroll snap or overscroll affordance on dense horizontal and vertical media surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Add platform-native snap or overscroll behavior only where it clarifies a carousel or drawer interaction.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not reflect scroll state
findings.evidence: The long homepage exposes no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or shrinking-header behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky, scroll-state-aware header or progress cue without obscuring content.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is not anchored or edge-aware
findings.evidence: The load screenshot shows a custom centered overlay; DOM inspection found no dialog, popover, or anchor-positioning primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a semantic top-layer primitive and edge-aware positioning rather than an unanchored custom layer.

findings.summary: Consent blocks the primary content on every fresh load
findings.evidence: Desktop, category, signup, and video screenshots all show a large consent panel obscuring the primary page before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the panel footprint, keep choices clear and equal, and preserve access to the page context.

findings.summary: The blocking consent panel is not exposed as a dialog
findings.evidence: DOM probing found zero dialog or role=dialog elements and zero popovers while the blocking consent UI was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking surface with dialog semantics, a programmatic name, focus management, Escape behavior, and explicit dismiss controls.

findings.summary: Promotions and navigation crowd out the media content
findings.evidence: The desktop first viewport is dominated by a consent panel, promotional strip, header and side chrome; the mobile capture leaves only a narrow content column.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce promotional chrome and prioritize the content grid and primary task in the initial viewport.

findings.summary: The 360px layout renders a 1024px-wide page
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured scrollWidth 1024px and 664px horizontal overflow at a 360px visual viewport; the screenshot shows a wide sidebar consuming most of the screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve and lay out a true narrow-screen view using fluid sizing, responsive navigation and no fixed 1024px canvas.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available space
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no container queries, while the mobile screenshot shows desktop sidebar and cards compressed into a 360px viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Make sidebar, grid, cards and banners respond to their container sizes, with viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch targets are inadequate
findings.evidence: The first focused link computed to outline-style none and no box shadow; Lighthouse also found target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible indicator and ensure interactive targets meet touch size and spacing guidance.

findings.summary: Primary content and actions are obscured at entry
findings.evidence: The first viewport places consent, age verification and promotion ahead of the video browsing task, and the 360px view exposes only a sliver of content.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the content purpose and next action immediately visible, with secondary legal and promotional surfaces taking less space.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP misses the good threshold
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.9s and scored performance 0.85; FCP was 2.4s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce render-blocking CSS and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Load work includes blocking main-thread tasks
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, longest 160.27ms, with 149.12ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Split long tasks and schedule non-critical work at lower priority.

findings.summary: The initial page ships a large, render-blocking dependency set
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 147 requests and 1.73MB transferred, including 61 scripts; Lighthouse estimated 1.05s savings from render-blocking resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts and styles, reduce request chains, and prioritize only LCP-critical resources.

findings.summary: Substantial CSS and JavaScript are unused at load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 57KiB unused CSS (up to 94.6% in one file) and 26KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route-specific bundles and load optional dependencies only when needed.

findings.summary: Controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two unnamed buttons, two unnamed links and nine visible-label/accessibility-name mismatches; the DOM probe also found an unlabeled icon button and filter input.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name matching its visible label.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail contrast requirements
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 13 color-contrast failures and links that rely on color alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground and background tokens to meet WCAG contrast and add non-color link cues.

findings.summary: Focus treatment and list semantics are unreliable
findings.evidence: Focused content had no visible outline, and Lighthouse found malformed list structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible keyboard focus and use valid list/landmark structure and logical focus order.

findings.summary: The mobile and zoom experience does not reflow
findings.evidence: The 360px capture overflows by 664px; Lighthouse also failed meta-viewport zoom and target-size checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user zoom, remove restrictive viewport settings on mobile output, and reflow content without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Image sizing and delivery metadata are incomplete
findings.evidence: The image audit found 29 of 36 images without dimensions, 12 oversized images, eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded and one missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources and appropriate lazy loading for media thumbnails.

findings.summary: Video pages omit structured data
findings.evidence: The representative video page had Open Graph tags but no JSON-LD, so machine-readable VideoObject details are absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD that matches visible content and canonical metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookies are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers lacked X-Content-Type-Options and a response Referrer-Policy; two first-party cookies lacked Secure and settings used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff and a restrictive Referrer-Policy, mark HTTPS cookies Secure, and avoid SameSite=None unless required.

findings.summary: The pre-consent load has a broad third-party footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence observed 16 third-party origins and requests to collector.xhamster.com and tsyndicate.com on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent third-party requests and document each necessary processor and data purpose.

findings.summary: Sign-up offers no passkey path
findings.evidence: The sign-up surface offers Google, X and email options; source and DOM probes found no WebAuthn or passkey affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys as a phishing-resistant sign-in and reauthentication option while retaining accessible fallbacks.

findings.summary: The defensive policy set is narrow
findings.evidence: CSP only declared frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and nosniff were absent, and Permissions-Policy allowed only client hints rather than restricting sensitive features.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing resource CSP, nosniff, restrictive referrer and permissions policies, preserving the existing HSTS and frame protections.

findings.summary: Arabic UI mixes non-localized compact number notation
findings.evidence: The Arabic listing renders compact counts such as “1.9M مشاهدات” and “16.2M”, mixing English compact notation into Arabic copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Format numbers and compact units with Intl.NumberFormat using the active Arabic locale.

findings.summary: Signup errors are visible but not programmatically tied to fields
findings.evidence: Empty signup produced Arabic messages, but inputs remained :valid with no aria-invalid and the assertive live region was empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate each message with its field, set aria-invalid, and announce the error summary after submission.

findings.summary: Email signup disables expected autofill
findings.evidence: The email field uses autocomplete=off and the password field is named new-password rather than using a complete, standards-based autocomplete token set.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=email and autocomplete=new-password with semantic input types and labels.

findings.summary: Thumbnail assets are often oversized or missing delivery hints
findings.evidence: The image audit found 12 oversized images, 16 legacy-format results, three without srcset and 29 without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Request thumbnails at rendered size, prefer modern formats, provide srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Initial rendering performs avoidable script and style work
findings.evidence: The page loaded 61 scripts; Lighthouse identified unused CSS/JS and the trace recorded two long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional personalization, analytics and offscreen work until needed and prioritize foreground content.

findings.summary: Third-party and script budgets are not constrained
findings.evidence: The initial load transferred 1.73MB across 147 requests, with 1.03MB of scripts and 16 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set budgets for third-party origins, JavaScript and media, then gate optional integrations behind consent and interaction.

findings.summary: Core search and signup capabilities are not machine-exposed
findings.evidence: The public site has search and signup flows, but probing found no WebMCP or registered agent-readable tools.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose carefully scoped, confirmable capabilities for search and account actions with clear safety boundaries.
